verifiable-quality-gates.why: the change is to a CI gate aggregator; its new rendering must provably detect a vacuous pass and not misreport a failure, with a test that fails if reverted.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added AGG #150 discrimination cases (vacuous renders ○+note; real ✓; failing-with-marker stays ✗) AND a vacuous-marker contract test that reads the aggregator's real regex and asserts every gate produces it, closing the review's end-to-end guard gap; recomputed the aggregator's manifest sha so parity/provenance/integrity stay consistent.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

architectural-decision-records.why: a deliberate change to how the required check reports, with a non-obvious mechanism (marker detection, exit code unchanged) and honest limits.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0089 (render a vacuous pass apart; ignore .githooks in scan gates; keep it a pass; marker-coupling guarded by a test).
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the aggregator is a .mjs behavior surface; the happy (real pass), the new (vacuous pass), and the adverse (failure that prints the marker) cases are enumerated.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: node:test cases asserting the rendered board and exit code for a vacuous pass, a real pass, and a failing-with-marker gate.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the risk is the aggregator's output + exit behavior; the test exercises the real aggregator over throwaway fixture gates at the layer that owns it.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: integration tests that build fixture gates (one printing the vacuous marker, one a real OK line, one failing) and assert the aggregator's rendered board + exit code.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug, and match the test type to the risk.

skeptical-audit.why: the ADR claims a vacuous pass is now distinguishable and names what the change does NOT do; those claims need an evidence state and a named limitation.
skeptical-audit.what: stated the honest limits in ADR-0089 (the aggregator keys on the gates' marker text - a coupling guarded by the discrimination test; capture buffers instead of streaming; the change does not alter any gate's scope nor turn a vacuous pass into a failure; retention-basis is a separate issue).
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a change to the required check's machinery (capture vs stream, new rendering, a recomputed manifest sha) must pass the four-questions review before done.
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context subagent review of the staged diff (fail-closed preserved, output not lost, sha consistent, detection sound); recorded in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no input, auth, secret, or file-handling control; the change is CI reporting (rendering a vacuous pass apart), not a security control.

pattern-selector.why: no design pattern; a capture-and-classify step added to the existing aggregation loop.

arch-encode.why: no new recurring rule file; the behavior is pinned by its own discrimination test.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, storage, migration, retention, or backup is touched; the untagged-pii gate's own scope is unchanged, only its vacuous pass is now visible.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system/data architecture or service-boundary change; CI aggregator rendering.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy mechanics, migration, flag, or rollback change.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, SLO, alert, or golden signal; a CI check's output.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user UI; the audience is CI readers, and the ○-vs-✓ distinction is covered by the ADR/CHANGELOG.
